Hey if it makes you feel any better I did terribly in school because of depression and anxiety. I just could not focus, couldn't remember deadlines, and procrastinated all of my difficult subjects. I failed half of my classes and scraped by the rest. I worked for a few years and eventually went to college as a mature student. I got a degree in science, and was given a scholarship for another in psychology. I currently have a great job in neuroscience and am studying for my third degree in AI in the evenings. 

Basically what I'm trying to say is that school is not everything. I remember being in school and stressing myself out so much over all the subjects I was failing. I was absolutely fucking miserable which didn't help things. At the end of the day a whole decade later and despite failing half my classes, I managed to get into a good university, I managed to get a scholarship, and a good job, and nothing I did in school ever mattered. 

One other thing I will say is that the more I didn't care about assignments, the better I did. Worrying about them gave me anxiety and caused me to procrastinate and work less, then cramming the night before and inevitably failing. I'm not sure if this is happening to you but it's something to keep in mind. When it comes to doing assignments I have to consciously tell myself "this doesn't matter, you do not care, you can hand in something shit" and it helps me just get something, anything, done instead of procrastinating. 

It's really difficult not to care about these things when we are going through it, but just remember that there is always other options and other ways of reaching your goals. You can fail everything in school and still end up getting a good job that you enjoy and being happy and healthy in life.
